input: Given question: What are the exemptions that can be claimed against taxable income under general rule of travel expenses? Option A: Outside normal work hours where work at home has started prior to undertaking travel: FCT v Collings (1976) Option B: By itinerant workers: FCT v Wiener (1978) Option C: By taxpayers who are required to carry bulky items to perform employment duties: FCT v Vogt (1975) Option D: To alternative workplaces on a temporary basis: FCT v Ballesty (1977). Option E: All of above The correct answer is Option E.
reference: Normally, a person can claim travel expenses outside of work. even though General rule states that travel expenses occurred between home and normal place of work is not deductible: Lunney v FCT; Hayley v FCT.
best_explanation: Travel expenses: general rules and exemptions (continued) Under the general rules, the following exemptions can be claimed against taxable income: 1. Outside normal work hours where work at home has started prior to undertaking travel: FCT v Collings (1976)2. By itinerant workers: FCT v Wiener (1978)3. By taxpayers who are required to carry bulky items to perform employment duties: FCT v Vogt (1975)4. To alternative workplaces on a temporary basis: FCT v Ballesty (1977). 5. Uniform expenses: section 25-10 ITAA97 6. Expenses of travelling to and from work, unless taxpayer is a truck driver or delivery van driver: FCT v Ballesty (1978) 7. Expenses of travelling between home and work are generally not deductible: Lunney v FCT (1958) 8. For taxpayers who are not employees, deductions for travelling to work are limited to 1,000 small business entities: s 13-1 ITAA97 9. Deduction allowed for additional travel expenses of a person who is required to travel further than his or her usual place of work: FCT v Ballesty (1977). 10. All of above (1-9) Chapter 14 (Barakoczy, 2017) Travel expenses: general rules and exemptions Reference:Barkoczy, S.
